edits.target: 4. Domain has NO key and all its mandatory args are known -> first search (`x = search_*(...)` then `save_to_cache`).
edits.content: 4b. Domain has NO key and a mandatory arg is missing (hotel: check-in AND check-out dates; flight: departure date; restaurant: city) -> the ONLY output is one short `seek_information(...)` naming just the missing items. This holds on a first turn (CACHE `{}`). It also holds when the reply only gives hotel budget, stars, amenities or party size while the CACHE has only another domain (e.g. 'attractions'). Never run filter_hotels (or any filter) on another domain's cache key, never search with guessed or TOOL CONFIG example dates, and never add num_people, flight_class or num_layovers to search_flights. Correct whole output for 'a hotel in Tucson with a view of the ocean' (CACHE `{}`): `seek_information("We need the check-in and check-out dates for the hotel.")`, with no search_hotels call.

edits.target: ## Rule 7: Writing seek_information, including multi-domain requests
edits.content: - Name only the domain(s) the user actually requested. A flight-only opener with origin and destination ('large group booking from Atlanta to Tucson for a school trip') -> ask only for the departure date, and do not add hotel dates because no hotel was requested. A trip opener with origin and destination but no service named ('a weekend getaway to St. Louis from San Jose') implies a flight -> ask for the departure date. A hotel-only opener ('last-minute hotel deal in Fresno for 4 people', 'hotel in Tucson with an ocean view') -> ask only for check-in and check-out dates. Party size, occasion words and timing words ('last-minute', 'weekend', 'school trip') never fill a date or trigger a search.

edits.target: ## CACHE GATE (run this before writing any code, every turn)
edits.content:
0. SCOPE AND ROUTE FIRST. Read the assistant's LAST question and the user's reply: the reply belongs to that one domain. Name the domain of each constraint in the LAST turn: stars / amenity / hotel service / neighborhood / per-night budget / rooms -> hotels; cuisine / dietary / per-person budget / restaurant rating -> restaurants; attraction type or name -> attractions; class / airline / flight time / ticket budget -> flights. Look up that domain's OWN key in CACHE, write code only for that domain (plus any domain the reply newly requests), and never load or filter another domain's key to apply the reply. Other cached domains are finished: never reload, re-filter or re-save them because an earlier turn mentioned a class, budget or amenity. Before filtering, read the summary of the key you load. Anything it shows ('flight classes: [business]', 'Additionally filtering for budget: $300', 'has_gluten_free_options', 'neighborhood(s): [...]') is already applied and is never passed again.
   - CACHE 'departure_flights' and 'return_flights' (both show 'flight classes: [business]') + 'hotels' (shows Midtown Atlanta); the assistant asked the hotel budget and the user says 'Around 125.' -> exactly `h = get_results_from_cache(key="hotels")`, `h2 = filter_hotels(prior_results=h, budget=125)`, `save_to_cache(key="filtered_hotels", value=h2)`. No flight lines at all.
   - CACHE 'restaurants' (summary: 'neighborhood(s): [Midtown Atlanta], cuisine(s): [Livonian], has_gluten_free_options') + 'I'm looking to spend around 125 per person' -> `filter_restaurants(prior_results=r, budget=125)` only. Do not add has_gluten_free_options, even though the user said 'gluten-free' earlier.
   - Hotel service or amenity words ('room service and shuttle service', wifi, gym) answer a hotel question: load the most refined hotels key, `filter_hotels(prior_results=h, has_room_service=True, airport_shuttle_present=True)`, save under a new key (e.g. final_hotels). Never filter restaurants or flights for it, even if restaurant rating or cuisine came up earlier.
   - A hotel refinement in a flight + hotel conversation touches ONLY hotels. Example: CACHE flights/return_flights (class first) + hotels, last turn 'A 3 star hotel in Summerlin with business facilities' -> `h = get_results_from_cache(key="hotels")`, `h2 = filter_hotels(prior_results=h, neighborhood=["Summerlin"], stars=[3, 3])`, `save_to_cache(key="filtered_hotels", value=h2)` and nothing else. Here the 'hotels' summary already lists the business center, so it is not re-passed. When the summary does NOT list it, 'business facilities' maps to has_business_center=True (see Rule 27).
   - A party-size-only reply ('There are 5 of us') when NO hotel has been requested adds no constraint, because flight and restaurant tools have no party-size parameter. Write no search and no filter. At most `x = get_results_from_cache(key="<flight key>")` for each cached flight key.
   - Domain has NO key and its mandatory args are known anywhere in the conversation (hotel check-in/check-out may be the outbound/return flight dates; the city is the destination) -> first search NOW, carrying every constraint stated in any turn. Example: CACHE holds only flight keys (depart May 16, 2025, return May 18, 2025, trip to St. Louis) and the turn says 'A 4 star hotel in Downtown St. Louis with business facilities and a gym. And I'm interested in Touristy attractions' -> `hotels = search_hotels(city="St. Louis", checkin_date=["May 16, 2025"], checkout_date=["May 18, 2025"], stars=[4, 4], has_business_center=True, gym_present=True, neighborhood=["Downtown St. Louis"])` + save 'hotels', then `attractions = search_attractions(city="St. Louis", type=["Touristy"])` + save 'attractions'. Do NOT re-filter the flights.
   - Domain has NO key and a mandatory arg is missing (hotel with no check-in/check-out date) -> the ONLY output is one seek_information. Example: CACHE holds only 'attractions' (Las Vegas, Scenic), the user wants a hotel for 5 and now says 'We're looking for a 3 star hotel' -> `seek_information("We need the check-in and check-out dates for the hotel.")` and nothing else. Never apply a hotel reply to the attractions key.

ranking_details.reasoning: I ranked by recurring failure pattern, breadth, and how little each edit duplicates the existing rules. [3] and [6] have the highest support (8 each). Both target the same widespread error: searching or filtering with missing mandatory args, or asking for the wrong domain's items. [3] makes a missing mandatory arg on an uncached domain produce only seek_information, and bars filtering another domain's key. That check sits in the CACHE GATE, which is run every turn. [6] limits seek_information to the domains the user actually requested and says party size, occasion and timing words never supply dates. The two are complementary: [3] works at the cache-gate level and [6] at the Rule 7 wording level. For the third slot I chose [0] over [1]. [0] states the general principle that a reply belongs to one domain and is routed to that domain's own cache key. It also says to drop filters the cache summary already lists. Those are common refinement-turn failures, and [0] puts the scoping check at the top of the CACHE GATE. [1] has the same support but bundles many items that mostly repeat Rules 9, 24 and 7. [2], [4], [5], [7] and [8] have low support or are narrow. [9] and [10] are useful but cover a smaller set of failures.
